transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm really just here because people keep telling me I'm way too thin and need help, but I honestly don't see what the big problem is with my weight being this low. My friends and an urgent care doctor got really worried about it, but to me, it feels like they're completely overreacting.
Do you think your weight is normal or is there a possibility that you might be underweight, even if you don't feel that way?

I mean, I know my clothes are hanging off me and my belt is on the last hole, so I guess I might technically be underweight. But I don't see it as a problem—to me, it just feels like I'm really lean, disciplined, and running efficiently. I think everyone else is just blowing it way out of proportion.
Do you often find yourself restricting the amount of food you eat or purging after meals to maintain what you consider an ideal weight or body shape?

I do restrict my food quite a bit, usually just getting by on black coffee during the day and maybe a granola bar at night to save money and time while painting. It actually gives me a real sense of pride and discipline to eat so little, and the thought of gaining weight honestly panics me, but I definitely don't purge or anything like that.
Do you ever look in the mirror and see yourself as others describe you, underweight, or do you see a different body shape or weight than what others are concerned about?

When I look in the mirror, I don't see myself as dangerously underweight at all. I just zero in on my stomach or thighs and feel like they aren't razor-thin enough, which makes me feel like I've lacked discipline. I honestly think everyone is overreacting to how I look.

Do you have a strong desire to lose even more weight, despite others' concerns about your current weight, and do you believe that achieving a lower weight will significantly improve your life or self-worth?

Yeah, I do still think I could drop a few more pounds to be truly lean, even though everyone else thinks that's crazy. Keeping my weight low feels like the ultimate proof of my self-discipline, and if I see any part of my body that isn't razor-thin, I just feel like a total failure.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'razor-thin' and how that ideal body image affects your daily life and decisions about eating and exercise?

To me, "razor-thin" means looking in the mirror and wanting my stomach and thighs to have absolutely no softness, feeling like a failure if they aren't completely flat. This image drives a constant fear of gaining weight, so I avoid eating normal foods like burgers or pizza with friends out of panic that I'll wake up looking softer or heavier. It just pushes me to want to lose even more weight so I can maintain that disciplined, lean look.

Do you believe that if you were to gain a small amount of weight, even just a few pounds, you would immediately notice a significant change in your body shape or appearance that would be unacceptable to you?

Yes, absolutely. Even the thought of gaining just a few pounds triggers a massive panic that I'll wake up the next morning looking softer and heavier. I already scrutinize my stomach and thighs in the mirror, so any weight gain would make me feel like a total, undisciplined failure.
